findings.claim_or_location: Bibliography [12] Sayed 2021 iAge, tagged '[cohort; mouse/in-vitro mechanism components]'
findings.issue: The rubric requires every cite to carry exactly one enum type-tag. The body correctly distinguishes the two designs within this paper ('[12, cohort]' for the human immunome association and '[12, animal] [population-mismatch: mouse and human cell lines]' for the CXCL9 mechanism), but the bibliography line appends a free-text qualifier ('; mouse/in-vitro mechanism components') alongside the [cohort] enum, so the bibliography entry does not present a single clean enum type-tag.
findings.recommended_fix: Split [12] into two bibliography lines (one [cohort] for the human immunome cohort, one [animal] for the CXCL9 mouse/cell mechanism), or keep a single [cohort] enum on the bibliography line and move the 'mouse/in-vitro mechanism components' qualifier into the body annotation only, so each bibliography entry carries exactly one enum tag.

findings.claim_or_location: Finding 11, VO2max claim grounded in [21] Strasser & Burtscher 2018, Frontiers in Bioscience (Landmark) — bibliography self-flags '[mechanism_review; lower-trust publisher — flagged]'
findings.issue: Finding 11 is billed as the 'strongest, most replicated, and most modifiable' mortality links, yet the VO2max/cardiorespiratory-fitness pillar of that finding rests on a narrative review from a publisher the section itself flags as lower-trust, rather than a primary cohort or meta-analysis. The gait [18] and grip [19,20] claims in the same finding are anchored to Tier-1 primaries/meta-analyses; the VO2max claim is comparatively weakly grounded for a 'strongest evidence' designation.
findings.recommended_fix: Substitute or add a Tier-1/2 primary or meta-analysis for the VO2max-mortality association (e.g., a high-trust cardiorespiratory-fitness cohort or meta-analysis with a reported HR), so the strongest functional-marker finding rests uniformly on admissible-tier evidence and does not lean on a flagged-publisher review.
